title: Polynomial-time computable branching
statement:
Let $p:
\{0,1\}^*\to\{0,1\}$ and $f,g:
\{0,1\}^*\to\{0,1\}^*$ be polynomial-time computable, where $p$ is computed as a one-bit output word. Then the function sending $x$ to $f(x)$ when $p(x)$ is true and to $g(x)$ otherwise is polynomial-time computable.
hypotheses_covered: The one-bit-valued function $p$ is polynomial-time computable
replaced: Let $p$ be a Boolean-valued predicate on bit strings and let $f, g$ be functions from bit strings to bit strings. Suppose that the map sending $x$ to the one-bit word $p(x)$ is polynomial-time computable, and that $f$ and $g$ are polynomial-time computable (each computed by some finite binary Turing machine within $C(n+1)^c$ steps on inputs of length $n$, for some constants $C, c$). Then the map sending $x$ to $f(x)$ if $p(x)$ is true and to $g(x)$ otherwise is polynomial-time computable.
